note: All figures are FACT, transcribed from J&J results releases in sources.json/signals.json. Interpretations are labeled ai_hypothesis and separated from fact.

fact.franchise_highlights: Darzalex $14.4bn (+23.0%); Tremfya $5.2bn (+40.5%); Carvykti $1.9bn (+95.9%); Stelara $6.1bn (-41.3% on biosimilar erosion).

quarters.ai_hypothesis: A ~$94bn base with fast-compounding Tremfya/Darzalex/Carvykti offsetting Stelara's collapse implies budget concentration on replacement-asset launches and oncology support.
Accelerating Q4 growth exiting 2025 sets up the $100bn 2026 revenue crossing.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.note: Slower-growing segment; cardiovascular (Abiomed, Shockwave) is the fastest-growing pillar.

fact.franchise_highlights: Tremfya $2.046bn worldwide; Darzalex $4.207bn worldwide; Carvykti $657M (+); Stelara $740M (declining).

quarters.ai_hypothesis: Innovative Medicine materially outpaces MedTech; MedTech underperformance opens a commercial-modernization opening while pharma launches drive the growth.

fact.milestone: On track to surpass $100bn annual revenue for the first time in J&J's 140-year history
fact.eps_dilution_note: $0.15 dilution to 2026 adjusted EPS from the $3.05bn Halda Therapeutics acquisition (short-term financing + non-recurring charge).

guidance.ai_hypothesis: Repeated Q1 and Q2 guidance raises signal management confidence and sustained-to-growing commercialization budgets, de-risking multi-year vendor commitments.
